items.cite: Bálint András Varga, *Conversations with Iannis Xenakis* (Faber and Faber, 1996).
items.note: Two interviews with Xenakis, of 1980 and 1989, in which he spoke about his wartime years, Le Corbusier’s studio, Messiaen and the making of Metastaseis.

items.cite: Iannis Xenakis, *Formalized Music: Thought and Mathematics in Composition*, revised edition, edited by Sharon Kanach (Pendragon Press, 1992).
items.note: His own account of how probability, set theory and sieves entered his scores, from Pithoprakta and Achorripsis to Nomos Alpha and stochastic synthesis.

items.cite: Sharon Kanach and Peter Nelson, eds., *Meta-Xenakis: New Perspectives on Iannis Xenakis’s Life, Work, and Legacies* (Open Book Publishers, 2024).
items.note: The volume has more than fifty chapters, among them Guy Pimienta on Le Corbusier’s studio (chapter 22) and Erik Christensen and Lise Bjerno on Pithoprakta (chapter 18).

items.cite: Charles Turner, *Xenakis in America* (One Block Avenue, 2014).
items.note: Xenakis in the United States: Tanglewood in 1963, performances of Pithoprakta under Bernstein and Copland, and the Indiana years, documented from archives.

items.cite: Dimitris Exarchos, ed., *A Xenakis Dictionary* (Les Amis de Xenakis, 2023).
items.note: Signed entries explaining his terms, from sieve theory and ruled surfaces to the UPIC and the polytopes, each with references.

items.cite: Marc Treib, *Space Calculated in Seconds: The Philips Pavilion, Le Corbusier, Edgard Varèse* (Princeton University Press, 1996).
items.note: A study of the 1958 Philips pavilion that covers how it was conceived and built and treats its architecture, its film and Varèse’s tape together.
